chapter.name: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry

subtopics.name: Acidic and Basic Strength of Organic Compounds

questions.stem:
The correct order of increasing basic strength of the following amines in aqueous solution is:
(I) $\mathrm{CH_3NH_2}$
(II) $\mathrm{(CH_3)_2NH}$
(III) $\mathrm{(CH_3)_3N}$
(IV) $\mathrm{NH_3}$
questions.solution: For methyl-substituted amines in aqueous medium, the order of basic strength is governed by inductive effect, steric hindrance, and solvation. The experimentally determined order of basicity is: $\mathrm{(CH_3)_2NH} > \mathrm{CH_3NH_2} > \mathrm{(CH_3)_3N} > \mathrm{NH_3}$. Thus, $\text{IV} < \text{III} < \text{I} < \text{II}$.

questions.stem:
Among the following compounds, the total number of compounds which are more acidic than phenol is ________.
Propan-1-ol, $o$-Nitrophenol, $m$-Nitrophenol, $p$-Nitrophenol, Ethanol, $o$-Cresol
questions.solution:
Acidic strength of nitro-substituted phenols is higher than phenol because of the electron-withdrawing $-\text{I}$ and $-\text{M}$ effects of the $-\text{NO}_2$ group.
Thus, $o$-nitrophenol, $m$-nitrophenol, and $p$-nitrophenol are all more acidic than phenol.
Propan-1-ol and ethanol are weaker acids than phenol because phenoxide ion is resonance stabilized.
$o$-Cresol is less acidic due to the electron-donating methyl group ($+\text{I}$ and hyperconjugation).
Therefore, there are exactly 3 compounds more acidic than phenol.

questions.stem:
Arrange the following compounds in decreasing order of basic strength:
(I) Aniline
(II) $p$-Nitroaniline
(III) $p$-Toluidine
(IV) $p$-Anisidine
questions.solution:
Basic strength depends on electron density on the nitrogen. 
- $-\mathrm{OCH_3}$ group (in $p$-anisidine) is highly electron donating via $+M$ effect (strongest base).
- $-\mathrm{CH_3}$ group (in $p$-toluidine) is electron donating via $+I$ and hyperconjugation.
- Aniline is unsubstituted.
- $-\mathrm{NO_2}$ group (in $p$-nitroaniline) is strongly electron-withdrawing via $-M$ and $-I$ (weakest base).
Thus, the correct order is IV > III > I > II.

questions.stem:
Arrange the following compounds in decreasing order of their basic strength:
(I) Aniline  
(II) $p$-Nitroaniline  
(III) $p$-Methylaniline  
(IV) $p$-Methoxyaniline  

Choose the correct option:
questions.solution:
Electron-donating groups increase the basic strength of aniline, while electron-withdrawing groups decrease it.  
- $-\mathrm{OCH_3}$ (in IV) is a strong $+M$ group (highest basic strength).  
- $-\mathrm{CH_3}$ (in III) is $+I$ and hyperconjugative (higher than aniline).  
- Aniline (I) has no substituents.  
- $-\mathrm{NO_2}$ (in II) is a strong $-M$ group (lowest basic strength).  
Hence, order is IV > III > I > II.

questions.stem:
Among the following compounds, the total number of compounds which are more acidic than benzoic acid is ____________.
- $o$-Nitrobenzoic acid
- $p$-Nitrobenzoic acid
- $p$-Methoxybenzoic acid
- $o$-Toluic acid
- $p$-Toluic acid
- $o$-Bromobenzoic acid
questions.solution:
Due to ortho-effect, ortho-substituted benzoic acids ($o$-nitrobenzoic acid, $o$-toluic acid, $o$-bromobenzoic acid) are more acidic than benzoic acid.
For para-substituted:
- $p$-Nitrobenzoic acid has strong electron-withdrawing $-M$ and $-I$ effects, making it more acidic than benzoic acid.
- $p$-Methoxybenzoic acid is less acidic than benzoic acid due to $+M$ effect of $-\mathrm{OCH_3}$.
- $p$-Toluic acid is less acidic than benzoic acid due to $+I$ and hyperconjugation of $-\mathrm{CH_3}$.
Thus, $o$-nitrobenzoic acid, $p$-nitrobenzoic acid, $o$-toluic acid, and $o$-bromobenzoic acid (total 4) are more acidic than benzoic acid.

questions.stem: Which of the following compounds has the highest acidic strength?
questions.solution: The nitro group ($-NO_2$) is a strong electron-withdrawing group showing $-M$ and $-I$ effects. In $p$-nitrophenol, the $-M$ effect of the $-NO_2$ group strongly stabilizes the phenoxide ion formed after deprotonation. In $m$-nitrophenol, only the $-I$ effect is active. $p$-Cresol has an electron-donating methyl group ($+I$, hyperconjugation) which destabilizes the conjugate base. Thus, $p$-nitrophenol is the most acidic.

questions.stem:
Among the following compounds, the total number of compounds containing at least one $sp^3$ hybridized carbon atom is _________.
Benzene, Cyclohexane, Toluene, Acetylene, Ethane, Nitrobenzene, Acetone, Phenol
questions.solution:
- Benzene: all $sp^2$
- Cyclohexane: all $sp^3$ (contains $sp^3$)
- Toluene: methyl carbon is $sp^3$ (contains $sp^3$)
- Acetylene: all $sp$
- Ethane: all $sp^3$ (contains $sp^3$)
- Nitrobenzene: all $sp^2$
- Acetone: two methyl carbons are $sp^3$ (contains $sp^3$)
- Phenol: all $sp^2$
Total compounds containing $sp^3$ hybridized carbons = 4 (Cyclohexane, Toluene, Ethane, Acetone).
